question.prompt: Consider the set of numbers \(\{1, 10, 10^2, 10^3, \ldots, 10^{10}\}.\) The ratio of the largest element of the set to the sum of the other ten elements of the set is closest to which integer?

solutions.explanation:
Multiplying the sum of the smaller elements by \(10\) shifts every power to the next one. Subtracting the original sum will then cancel the matching terms. Let \(S\) be that positive sum:
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=1+10+\cdots+10^9,\\
10S&=10+10^2+\cdots+10^{10}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting gives \(9S=10^{10}-1\), so \(10^{10}=9S+1\). The requested ratio is consequently
\[
\frac{10^{10}}{S}
=\frac{9S+1}{S}
=9+\frac1S.
\]
Because \(S>2\), we have \(0<1/S<1/2\). Thus the ratio lies strictly between \(9\) and \(9.5\), making its closest integer \(9\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Shift the powers and subtract
